prompt: A high-volume event-ingest service exports OpenTelemetry traces with 1% head sampling. During incidents, responders often have no trace for requests that exceeded 2 seconds or returned errors, while Prometheus memory is growing because metric labels include tenant_id and raw route values. Redesign and verify the production telemetry path without changing application business behavior: replace unbounded metric dimensions with bounded service/operation/status dimensions, preserve tenant/request correlation only in appropriate log/trace fields under the repository privacy policy, choose a documented head/tail sampling policy that retains the incident classes the team must diagnose, size/monitor the sampler pipeline, and build an SRE view over latency, traffic, errors, saturation/backlog, plus sampling/export health. Replay a deterministic corpus containing normal, >2s, and error requests and prove the retained traces and metric series satisfy the declared policy without presenting sampled trace counts as full request counts.

requirements: deterministic event-ingest corpus containing normal, slow, and error requests
OpenTelemetry collector/sampling configuration with inspectable emitted telemetry
Prometheus-compatible metric backend with series-count inspection
repository privacy policy fixture covering correlation identifiers

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The revised metric schema removes tenant_id/raw unbounded route values from label dimensions and the deterministic corpus produces a bounded series count consistent with the declared operation/status dimensions.
Request/tenant correlation is retained only in signals and fields permitted by the privacy policy and is not copied into metric labels or sensitive payload logging.

The documented sampling policy retains every required synthetic error and >2s incident-class trace in the replay corpus or explicitly records a bounded false-negative policy; the result does not assume 1% head sampling can inspect completed trace outcomes.
The collector/sampler exposes capacity, drop/export failure, and queue/backpressure health needed to detect when the sampling pipeline cannot honor its policy.
Dashboards use unsampled metric/event counters for full request traffic/error denominators and do not present retained trace counts as population request counts.

requiredEvidence: bounded metric schema and observed series counts
sampling policy and deterministic retained/dropped trace inventory
